term: disjoint-world duplication of a local grounding structure
definition: A typed LocalState supplies independent existence, concreteness and binary grounding relations on one rigid candidate carrier. The 'doubled' operation builds two mutually accessible possible-world histories. Individuals are rigid pairs (world-tag, source-individual); each exists only in its tagged world, while its concreteness status and world-local causal/grounding edges copy the source structure. The construction preserves the stated local properties under their exact antecedents, but does not establish metaphysical possibility, source authenticity or a counterpart identity theory.
note: Research schema for #505 / #487 / #495: diagnose attempts to derive a de re necessary concretum from intraworld population, local causality and well-foundedness alone. Additional modal identity, existential grounding or anti-brute principles require separate defense.
